state.context:
Assess a specific small-app composition repair in canlang. The language is generated by agents for business records, access rules and workflows, and aims at adoption through economical tokens, dependable output and a single notation for each primitive. Its user requests research through implementation after validation, stopping if a proposal is invalid. New wrapper packages solely to enable composition, source manifests and connection registries are not acceptable. A scan found 44 sources with 48 app declarations and 49 explicit packages. TeamTasks is the sole implicit app; app and package names do not intersect. No parser/runtime is available and neither generation quality nor tokenizer savings is measured. App names already have explicit project identity in a flat app/package namespace. Existing use groups import exported names, uses assembles apps/packages and contexts, and owning packages retain authoritative models, policies, roles and operations. A deployment selects one app with one UI and one MCP interface, independently of file placement.
Today each implicit body is called main, and the design bans selecting two of them together. Its tool spelling is main.Model.operation. One alternative retains that local spelling and adds aliases in composition. This gives explicit assembly labels, possibly short ones, and retains standalone tool names. Prefixing external tools alone does not distinguish internal model/role owners. Deriving those owners from assembly aliases fixes collisions but makes canonical identity depend on assembly and complicates duplicate paths and operation receipts. Another qualifies the hidden segment as App.main; it provides distinct packages stable through moves and composition, but requires dotted provider resolution and an extra segment, and still changes under app renames. Deferral is possible when a coherent choice has not been established. The rejected extra-wrapper solution is outside the alternatives.
The direct-name candidate assigns the implicit body the already authored app identifier. Application membership and package ownership are two views of one index entry, not duplicate declarations. Other named packages/apps with that identifier still conflict. use Tasks {Todo} resolves exported names from Tasks' implicit package with ordinary local or bound interface semantics; it does not import its app context or mount every page/tool. uses=[Tasks] selects the application with its context. A composed or explicitly packaged app has no aggregated package to import by its app name. Export visibility, role qualifications, permissions and canonical operations stay independent of selection. No new ownership store or data clone is synthesized.
Direct-name parsing permits multiple implicit apps per source: a bare app declaration has its optional context next, imports before Given, exactly one ordered complete Given/When/Then body, and ends at the next top-level app/package or EOF. uses and an implicit body cannot coexist on one app. Deduplication keys the owning package once across imports and nested product selections. Its qualified types, models, roles, events, handlers, schedules and operations remain the same when selected alone or through another app or moved between files. Team and parent inheritance, by/on source restrictions and storage bindings preserve their behavior. There is no automatic route/resource renaming; duplicate routes and conflicting explicit context remain diagnostics. Separate deployments keep separate runtime state. The cost is coupling implicit declarations to app identity: renaming the app changes API/storage declaration names, and extraction to an explicit equal-named package is impossible while the original equal-named app remains under the existing flat namespace. Explicit migration is needed, not inferred transfers or old-name aliases. Current sources contain no synthetic-main references; an unrelated main string is business data.
External primary references contribute limited principles: Go separates local import naming from package dependency and confines qualified access to imported exported symbols, without requiring canlang to adopt its directory rules. MCP's tool guidance permits dots in names and recommends per-server uniqueness, case sensitivity and a limited ASCII character set. Neither proves canlang execution or selects a namespace automatically. Compare candidate advantages and liabilities rather than presuming a solution is safe.

examples.direct:
# Track work.
app Tasks
Given
 export Todo {title:text}
 role reviewer
 policy Todo read=members
When
 crud Todo by=members fields=title
Then
 page /tasks title="Tasks"
  list Todo
# Keep notes.
app Notes
Given
 Note {text:text}
 role reviewer
 policy Note read=members
When
 crud Note by=members fields=text
Then
 page /notes title="Notes"
  list Note
# Use both apps.
app Office uses=[Tasks,Notes]
examples.alias_composition: app Office uses=[Tasks as work,Notes as notes]
examples.diamond:
app Bundle uses=[Tasks,Notes]
app Office uses=[Tasks,Bundle]
examples.route_collision: Tasks declares page /; Notes declares page /

identity_choice.instructions: What should supply the implicit package identity under this evidence?

criteria.composer_alias: Retain local main and introduce composition aliases with explicit ownership-rekeying requirements.
criteria.unresolved: Postpone the namespace choice if none is sufficiently specified.
criteria.direct_app: Derive the implicit owner directly from its declared app identity, using the current import grouping.
criteria.app_main: Qualify main beneath the app identity and define dotted import-provider lookup.

direct_coherence.instructions: Do the proposed direct-name boundaries and resolution semantics consistently distinguish owning packages, app selection and authorization in the cases described?
